title: Pregnancy Nutrition in the UK: What the Evidence Actually Says
author: Bite Insight Team
excerpt: Folic acid, fish limits and a change coming to UK bread this winter: what the NHS really says about eating well in pregnancy.
meta_title: Pregnancy Nutrition in the UK: What Actually Matters | Bite Insight
meta_description: Folic acid, fish limits and a change coming to UK bread this winter. Here is what the NHS and the evidence actually say about eating well in pregnancy.
ai_summary: Pregnancy nutrition in the UK comes down to a short list of nutrients worth prioritising, folic acid at 400 micrograms daily, vitamin D at 10 micrograms, iron and omega 3, alongside a compact list of genuine food safety risks such as unpasteurised soft cheese, pate and raw eggs without the Lion stamp. From December 2026, UK law will require most wheat flour to be fortified with folic acid, expected to reduce neural tube defects by around 20 percent, though supplements remain essential in early pregnancy since fortification only supports rather than replaces that advice. Common worries like caffeine, alcohol, sushi and takeaways are addressed using actual NHS limits and food safety guidance rather than internet myth. Use Bite Insight with your profile set to pregnant to make it easier to spot ingredients worth double checking while you shop.
